factual_methodology.summary: Medieval scholarship and National Archives source framework; historical model numbers and periods expressly hypothetical, never misrepresented as measured population averages.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Distinct products: global/European medieval commercial economy versus narrower manorial rents and coercive rights, without conflating fief and manor.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two numeric-series charts with explicit pedagogical and sourcing caveats, evidence/measurement table, historical causal diagram and geography map; bilingual numerical agreement.

research_depth.summary: 14 analytic headings, 12 scholarly and archive references over 4 hosts.

evidence_traceability.summary: Cambridge, Oxford, Wiley and UK National Archives / history specialist references integrated; source URLs and modeling assumptions match across locales.

counterfactual_review.summary: Explicit contract-incidence examples show mechanisms rather than pretending to estimate medieval averages; pestilence and regional labour divergence assessed conditionally.

limitations: Numerical models are didactic, not empirical medieval averages
Spatial and legal diversity prohibits universal feudal GDP inference
notes: QA tied to exact pending and staged source blobs, subject to independent production build and deployment.
